requests.exact_question: Which repository-executable facts anchor the mechanism overview for dynamic graph encoding: specifically, which code paths and data structures demonstrate that raw interaction sequences are extracted, represented with heterogeneous feature channels (node identity, edge attributes, absolute timestamps, co-occurrence indicators), padded to a fixed length, and assembled into a unified multi-channel tensor prior to routing?

What repository evidence (code, documentation, or test) demonstrates that the downstream prediction stage reads out fixed-size node embeddings from the sequential SSM output and produces task-specific predictions for link prediction and node classification, including the specific pooling-and-MLP head architecture and any stated linear computational complexity bound?
current_known_facts: EdgeBank link-prediction pipeline: edge_bank_link_prediction writes positive_probabilities and negative_probabilities via predict_link_probabilities
edge_bank_unlimited_memory constructs edge_memories from full interaction history (src_node_ids, dst_node_ids)
predict_link_probabilities branches on membership in edge_memories, returning 1.0 or 0.0 per candidate
MEAN pooling over sequence dimension confirmed in DyGFormer and GraphMixer
No evidence shows an MLP head following mean-pooled embeddings for link prediction or node classification
No evidence confirms the linear computational complexity claim for the downstream adaptation stage
requests.why_needed_for_reader: The section heading promises an overview of how the downstream adaptation stage realizes both link prediction and node classification with a note on linear computational complexity, but no repository evidence currently anchors the mechanism_overview move that would connect the sequential SSM output to task-specific prediction heads and justify the complexity claim.
